sentences.text: Dated this the 4th day of June 2025
JUDGMENT

The aforesaid appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the 3 rd respondent/insurer in O.P.(MV) No.467/2013 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Neyyattinkara, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 07/05/2019.
The sole respondent herein is the claim petitioner in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claimant, on 06/11/2012 at about 03:15 p.m., while he was riding his motorcycle through Vizhinjam-Poovar public road and when he reached the place by name Kochuthara, truck bearing registration No.TN69AF9199 driven by the second 2025:KER:39115 MACA NO. 312 OF 2020 respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
The incident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the second respondent/driver of the truck.
Hence, a sum of 10,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The first respondent/owner and the second respondent/driver of the offending vehicle remained ex parte.
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the existence of a valid policy in respect of the offending vehicle.
It was contended that there was no negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver.
The age, occupation and income of the claim petitioner were disputed.
It was also contended that the compensation claimed was quite excessive.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts.A1 to A19 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No documentary evidence was produced by the respondents.

The Tribunal on a consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the second respondent-driver of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 11,97,500/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.

Aggrieved by the Award,
the third respondent/insurer has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

sentences.text: Heard both sides 9.
The learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer raised several arguments challenging the compensation awarded under various heads.
The claim petitioner herein was a 32 year old man who claimed an amount of 10,000/- as his monthly income.
He relied on Ext.A10 to substantiate his argument that he was running a poultry farm.

The Tribunal was not inclined to accept the 2025:KER:39115 MACA NO. 312 OF 2020 allegation of the claim petitioner on the basis of Ext.A10 and fixed the notional income of the claim petitioner as 6,000/-.
Going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Allian. Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236, the notional income of even a coolie in the year 2012 was liable to be fixed at 8,500/- per month.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Allian. Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That being the position, I find that the third respondent/insurer cannot have any grievance regarding the amount that has been fixed by the Tribunal.
Though the amount of compensation awarded under the other heads are also challenged, I do not find any reason(s) to interfere with the impugned award.
That being the position, the appeal sans merit is dismissed.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.

Sd/-
